    John Rodriguez Lage v. Attorney General United States of America (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-25-03361 / USCOURTS-ca3-25-03361-0

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals denied John Diego Rodriguez-Lage's petition for review of a final order of removal. The court affirmed the Board of Immigration Appeals' finding that the petitioner did not establish the statutory criteria for severe spousal mistreatment required for VAWA cancellation and dismissed other claims as unreviewable. The court further confirmed its jurisdiction to review agency applications of the statutory severe mistreatment standard, abrogating prior circuit precedent on that point. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 19:59:28 Eastern time ET
    Keidy Posada-Arriola, et al v. Attorney General United States of America (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-01095 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-01095-0

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals dismissed in part and denied in part a petition for review filed by Keidy Dallana Posada-Arriola and her children, seeking to reopen removal proceedings. The court affirmed the Board of Immigration Appeals' denial of the motion, finding it lacked jurisdiction to review the denial of sua sponte reopening as no incorrect legal premise or arbitrary departure from settled adjudication was present. The court also rejected the petitioners' due process claims. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the District Court's dismissal of Ronald Emrit's complaint against Sabrina Carpenter and others.     Matthew L. Stewart v. Nissan North America, Inc., et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-25-02790 / USCOURTS-ca7-25-02790-0

    FAPD-AI: The United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit affirmed a district court's grant of summary judgment in favor of Nissan North America, Inc., and Nissan Motor Acceptance Corporation. Plaintiff Matthew Stewart had alleged age discrimination under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act regarding his unsuccessful application for a new position (P5) after a company reorganization. The appellate court found insufficient evidence to establish that the P5 hiring decision was based on age discrimination, concluding that the hiring managers' belief in another candidate's qualifications was a legitimate reason. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca13-25-02024 / USCOURTS-ca13-25-02024-0

    FAPD-AI: The United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit reversed the Armed Services Board of Contract Appeals' dismissal of a complaint filed by Walsh Turner Joint Venture II against the Secretary of the Army. Walsh alleged increased costs from government actions related to Executive Order 14042, which had mandated COVID-19 safety protocols for federal contractors. The court found Walsh's complaint sufficiently alleged a constructive change to its contract and remanded the case for further proceedings, including analysis of the government’s sovereign-acts-doctrine defense. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Hangxiao Che, et al v. Daimler Truck North America LLC, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-26-01795 / USCOURTS-ca7-26-01795-0

    FAPD-AI: The Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals vacated summary judgments and determined that two consolidated tort suits lacked federal subject-matter jurisdiction. The court found that diversity jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. §1332(a)(2) does not permit suits between foreign nationals on one side and a mixture of state citizens and foreign nationals on the other. Consequently, the case originally filed in federal court was dismissed, and the case removed from state court was remanded without addressing personal jurisdiction, as the court rejected a "futility exception" to the statutory mandate for remand. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    official summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2018-26-01 for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. AD 2018-26-01 required initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. Since the FAA issued AD 2018-26-01, CFM issued updated service material providing improvements to the ultrasonic inspection procedures and expanding the inspection area. This AD requires initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-01

    official summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-08-51, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 D-3 helicopters. AD 2026-08-51 requires inspecting the rotor hub-shaft for cracks, replacing any rotor hub-shaft that has any crack, and reporting information after accomplishment of the replacement. AD 2026-08-51 also prohibits installing any affected rotor hub-shaft on any helicopter, unless certain requirements are met. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-08-51, it was determined that additional repetitive inspections (including eddy current inspections) are necessary, and that revising the compliance time to account for hoist operations is necessary. This proposed AD would retain the actions of AD 2026-08-51 and would require additional repetitive inspections. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.     official summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bell Textron Canada Limited (Bell) Model 429 helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of premature wear-out of certain spherical bearings due to a quality escape of the spherical bearing monoballs not receiving the required hard coating. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the tail rotor (TR) pitch link assemblies and their bearings for cracks, wear, and mechanical or corrosion damage and, depending on the results, replacing any affected TR pitch link assembly. This AD also allows an affected part to be installed in a helicopter if certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-01

    official summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-08-06 which applied to certain Airbus Helicopters Model SA330J helicopters. AD 2025-08-06 required repetitively inspecting for a gap between the main gearbox (MGB) oil cooling fan assembly rotor blade and the upper section of the guide vane bearing housing, replacing the MGB fan rotor bearings with serviceable bearings if necessary, and at a later compliance time replacing the MGB fan rotor bearing assembly with an improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, which constitutes terminating action for the repetitive inspections. Since AD 2025-08-06 was issued, the FAA determined that the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly should be extended. This AD continues to require the actions in AD 2025-08-06 and increases the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly. This AD also prohibits installing any MGB fan rotor bearings and any MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-01

    Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF LABOR · FR-2026-11-24 / 2026-23936

    official summary: In this proposed rule, the Department of Labor (Department) clarifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). The proposed rule affirms that ERISA's duty of loyalty requires fiduciaries to act with the exclusive purpose of ensuring retirement security and providing promised benefits to plan participants and their beneficiaries. The amendments clarify the neutral application of ERISA's fiduciary duties of prudence and loyalty to selecting investments and investment courses of action, and to exercising shareholder rights, including proxy voting, the use of written proxy voting policies and guidelines, and shareholder engagement activities. The amendments would enhance the regulation by adding an affirmative expression of the duty of loyalty that is more consistent with the statute, and removing the tiebreaker test and participant preference provisions, which do not comport with the best reading of the statute and are susceptible to abuse, including use by a fiduciary as pretext to employ plan assets to pursue personal preferences or objectives unrelated to financial benefits under the plan. [official summary truncated; see source] FR-SEL-02

    official summary: This action amends Class D and Class E airspace over Tri-Cities, TN. Specifically, this action modifies the Tri-Cities Class D and Class E surface area airspace by expanding the radius and lateral boundaries to the northeast and removing the Tri-Cities Class E surface area extension airspace to the northeast. Additionally, this action modifies the Tri-Cities Class E transitional airspace beginning at 700 feet above the surface by expanding the lateral boundaries of the western portion of the airspace. Lastly, this action updates the airport name within the Class D and E legal descriptions and other outdated verbiage. FR-SEL-01

  • Observed at 05:56:34 Eastern time ET
    Restructuring the Governance and Funding Model of the Consolidated Audit Trail (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION · FR-2026-11-24 / 2026-23951

    official summary: Although the consolidated audit trail (the “CAT”) continues to be a necessary regulatory tool, its decentralized governance has presented certain challenges to administering the CAT. To address those shortcomings, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission” or the “SEC”) proposes to assume direct control of the CAT. Specifically, the Commission is proposing amendments to Regulation NMS under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Exchange Act”) that would rescind Rule 613, which obligates the national securities exchanges and national securities associations (collectively, the “SROs”) to act jointly to develop a national market system plan to develop, implement, and maintain the CAT (the “CAT NMS Plan”). The Commission is simultaneously proposing new Rule 17a-26, which would require the SROs and broker-dealers to record and electronically report to a central repository substantially the same information that was previously required to be recorded and reported pursuant to Rule 613, the CAT NMS Plan, related SRO compliance rules, and related exemptive relief previously issued by the Commission. FR-SEL-02

    HR 2478 ENR: Financial Exploitation Prevention Act of 2025 (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr2478enr

    FAPD-AI: H.R. 2478, the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act of 2025, amends Section 22 of the Investment Company Act of 1940. Registered open-end investment companies and transfer agents that elect to comply may request contact information for an adult individual for non-institutional direct at-fund accounts, and may postpone redemption payments for more than seven days for up to 15 business days, extendable by 10 business days, when they reasonably believe financial exploitation of a specified adult has occurred, is occurring, or was attempted. The Act also directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to submit a report with regulatory and legislative recommendations to Congress within one year of enactment. BILLS-SEL-01

The bill authorizes $84,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 and directs the USGS Director to give preference, to the extent practicable, to United States-owned and United States-controlled contractors. The bill passed the House on November 18, 2026, and was placed on the Senate calendar on November 19, 2026. BILLS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: H.R. 973, the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act, directs the Consumer Product Safety Commission to promulgate, within 180 days of enactment, ANSI/CAN/UL 2271, ANSI/CAN/UL 2849, and ANSI/CAN/UL 2272 as consumer product safety standards, limited to consumer products as defined in the Consumer Product Safety Act. The Act treats revisions to these voluntary standards as Commission standards effective 180 days after the standards organization notifies the Commission, unless the Commission determines within 90 days that the revision does not improve safety. The Commission must also report to Congress within five years of enactment on fires, explosions, and other hazards involving lithium-ion batteries in micromobility products. BILLS-SEL-01

    FAPD-AI: S. 2883, the Quantifying Uncertainty and Action to Help Optimize Growth of Shellfish Act of 2025 or QUAHOGS Act of 2025, was introduced by Senator Whitehouse and reported by Senator Cruz with an amendment on November 20, 2026. The bill directs the Secretary of Commerce to convene an East Coast Bivalve Research Task Force of 16 to 21 members within 90 days of enactment to review bivalve research, identify applied research needs for quahogs (hard clams) and other bivalves, and support sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. The Task Force must submit an interim progress report within one year and a final report within two years, and it is required to establish work groups, including one on quahog research needs in Rhode Island and across the East Coast and one on climate change impacts. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 for completed, fully assembled semiconductor manufacturing equipment and ineligible semiconductor manufacturing equipment made, assembled, or refurbished by foreign entities of concern or their subsidiaries or affiliates.     FAPD-AI: S. 3954, the No Lifeline for Dead People Act, as reported with an amendment by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, would prohibit an eligible telecommunications carrier from providing Lifeline service to a consumer unless the National Verifier has been used to verify the consumer's eligibility and the carrier has used the National Lifeline Accountability Database to determine that the service would not violate restrictions on duplicative support. The bill directs the Federal Communications Commission to coordinate with the Treasury Department on the Do Not Pay Initiative to help prevent Lifeline enrollments of deceased individuals and duplicative support. It also requires a Government Accountability Office study within 18 months of enactment on Lifeline program integrity and enrollment barriers, and an annual FCC report to Congress on eligible, enrolled, denied, abandoned, and disenrolled households. Digital certificates would be presented under authentication and verification requirements established by the Administrator. The bill directs the FAA Administrator to issue a final rule by November 30, 2028, updating parts 61, 63, 65, 67, and 107 of title 14, Code of Federal Regulations, to implement the amendment.     119 S69 RS: Curtailing Online Limitations that Lead Unconstitutionally to Democracy's Erosion Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119s69rs

    FAPD-AI: S. 69, the "Curtailing Online Limitations that Lead Unconstitutionally to Democracy's Erosion Act" or "COLLUDE Act," was introduced by Mr. Schmitt on January 9, 2025, referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, and reported by Mr. Cruz on November 20, 2026, with an amendment striking all after the enacting clause. The bill amends Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 230) to add a burden-of-proof provision for certain actions, to deny Section 230(c) protection to providers that restrict legitimate political speech as a result of certain governmental communications, and to define related terms, with exceptions for legitimate law enforcement and national security purposes. The text also defines "covered provider" as a social media platform with at least $250,000,000 in revenue in the preceding 12 months or at least 10,000,000 global monthly active users for three of the preceding 12 months, makes a "prohibited content action" by such a provider unlawful, and authorizes civil actions by affected information content providers with statutory damages, including the greater of $1,000,000 or three times compensatory damages in specified cases. BILLS-SEL-01
